value.zh: 五禮之別，二曰凶。
value.en: Among the five canonical rituals, the second category is mourning for the dead.
value.literal: Of the five kinds of ritual, the second is called 'inauspicious' (mourning).

value.zh: 自天子至於庶人，身體髮膚，受之父母，其理既均，其情亦等，生則養，死則哀，故曰三年之喪，天下之達禮者也。
value.en: From the sovereign to the humblest subject, flesh and hair come from one's parents; the duty is the same and the grief no different—while they live we sustain them, when they die we mourn them. Hence the canon calls three years' mourning the rite that runs through all the world.
value.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, body, skin, and hair are received from father and mother; the principle is uniform and the feeling equal—in life they nurture, in death they mourn; therefore it is said that three years' mourning is the penetrating rite of the realm.

value.zh: 漢禮，天子崩，自不豫至於登遐及葬，喪紀之制，與夫三代變易。
value.en: Han court precedent for an emperor's death—from the first illness through the lying-in-state to interment—shifted its mourning code across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou models.
value.literal: Under Han ritual, when the Son of Heaven collapsed, from the first illness through the final journey to burial, the mourning regulations changed with the Three Dynasties.

value.zh: 魏晉以來，大體同漢。
value.en: From the Wei through the Jin, the dynasty largely kept Han practice.
value.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, the broad pattern matched Han.

value.zh: 然自漢文革喪禮之制，後代遵之，無復三年之禮。
value.en: Yet once Emperor Wen of Han pared the mourning statutes, every succeeding age copied his shortcut, and the full three-year observance disappeared.
value.literal: Yet from Emperor Wen of Han's reform of mourning regulations, later ages followed it and no longer practiced three years' mourning.

value.zh: 及魏武臨終，遺令「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。
value.en: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.
value.literal: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.

value.zh: 百官當臨中者，十五舉音，葬畢便除。
value.en: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.
value.literal: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.

value.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。」
value.en: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'
value.literal: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'

value.zh: 魏武以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯，是月丁卯葬，是為不逾月也。
value.en: Cao Cao died on the gengzi day of the first month; by xinchou the bier stood ready; dingmao that same month saw the interment—mourning lifted inside a single month.
value.literal: Wei Wu died on gengzi in the first month; on xinchou he was encoffined; on dingmao that same month he was buried—this is what is meant by 'not exceeding one month.'

value.zh: 及宣帝、景帝之崩，並從權制。
value.en: The deaths of Sima Yi and Sima Shi were handled under the same shortened schedule.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan and Emperor Jing died, each likewise followed the expedient code.

value.zh: 文帝之崩，國內服三日。
value.en: When Sima Zhao died, the whole state wore mourning for three days and no more.
value.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the realm observed mourning for three days only.

value.zh: 武帝亦遵漢魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。
value.en: Emperor Sima Yan kept the Han–Wei rule of ending court mourning at burial, but he still dressed in plain hemp deep robes, set aside brocade cushions, and ate only coarse fare.
value.literal: Emperor Wu likewise followed Han and Wei precedent: once the burial ended he set aside formal mourning, yet still wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich food from his table.

value.zh: 大晉紹承漢魏，有革有因，期於足以興化而已，故未得皆返太素，同規上古也。
value.en: Great Jin inherits Han and Wei with some reforms and some continuities, aiming only to lift custom where it must; therefore it cannot yet return wholesale to pristine antiquity or match high antiquity in a single stroke.
value.literal: Great Jin inherits Han and Wei with some reforms and some continuities, aiming only to lift custom where it must; therefore it cannot yet return wholesale to pristine antiquity or match high antiquity in a single stroke.

value.zh: 陛下既以俯遵漢魏降喪之典，以濟時務，而躬蹈大孝，情過乎哀，素冠深衣，降席撤膳，雖武丁行之于殷世，曾閔履之於布衣，未足以逾。
value.en: Your Majesty has already bowed to Han and Wei's lowered mourning canons to meet pressing affairs, yet you personally tread the utmost filial path; your feeling overshoots moderation—plain cap, deep garments, lowered mat, curtailed meals—even King Wuding in the Yin age or Zengzi and Min Ziqian as commoners did not surpass this.
value.literal: Your Majesty has already bowed to Han and Wei's lowered mourning canons to meet pressing affairs, yet you personally tread the utmost filial path; your feeling overshoots moderation—plain cap, deep garments, lowered mat, curtailed meals—even King Wuding in the Yin age or Zengzi and Min Ziqian as commoners did not surpass this.

value.zh: 方今荊蠻未夷，庶政未乂，萬機事殷，動勞神慮，豈遑全遂聖旨，以從至情。
value.en: Now the southern tribes are not yet pacified, government is not yet ordered, and myriad threads of business press upon you, taxing mind and spirit—how could you wholly indulge sage intent and the utmost of private feeling?
value.literal: Now the southern tribes are not yet pacified, government is not yet ordered, and myriad threads of business press upon you, taxing mind and spirit—how could you wholly indulge sage intent and the utmost of private feeling?

value.zh: 臣等以為陛下宜割情以康時濟俗，輒敕御府易服，內省改坐，太官復膳，諸所施行，皆如舊制。」
value.en: We your servants therefore believe Your Majesty should cut private feeling to heal the age and aid custom; we dare order the Palace Treasury to exchange garments, the inner apartments to restore seating, the Grand Provisioner to restore full meals, and every other measure to follow the standing regulations.'
value.literal: We your servants therefore believe Your Majesty should cut private feeling to heal the age and aid custom; we dare order the Palace Treasury to exchange garments, the inner apartments to restore seating, the Grand Provisioner to restore full meals, and every other measure to follow the standing regulations.'

value.zh: 詔曰：「每感念幽冥，而不得終苴絰於草土，以存此痛，況當食稻衣錦，誠詭然激切其心，非所以相解也。
value.en: The edict replied: 'Whenever I brood on the shades below and realize I cannot finish wearing straw cord on the burial mound to keep this pain alive—how much more to eat polished rice and wear brocade—indeed it stabs the heart; that is no way to console myself.

value.en: I was born to a house of scholars; the rites have been handed down among us a long time—how could my heart one morning cast off this feeling toward him who is my heaven!
value.literal: I was born to a house of scholars; the rites have been handed down among us a long time—how could my heart one morning cast off this feeling toward him who is my heaven!

value.zh: 相從已多，可試省孔子答宰我之言，無事紛紜也。
value.en: You have followed me long; try reviewing Confucius's answer to Zai Wo—do not fuss at me again and again.
value.literal: You have followed me long; try reviewing Confucius's answer to Zai Wo—do not fuss at me again and again.

value.en: When words touch grief it tears the heart—what can be done!

value.en: Fu and the others rememorialized: 'We have read the sage edict and are moved to grief; we reflect on why Confucius checked Zai Wo's question—the sage mind cannot stop itself; the feeling is very deep and very earnest.

value.zh: 然今者干戈未戢，武事未偃，萬機至重，天下至眾。
value.en: Yet now weapons are not yet stilled, military affairs not yet rested, the myriad threads are weightiest, and all under Heaven is most numerous.
value.literal: Yet now weapons are not yet stilled, military affairs not yet rested, the myriad threads are weightiest, and all under Heaven is most numerous.

value.zh: 陛下以萬乘之尊，履布衣之禮，服粗席稿，水飲疏食，殷憂內盈，毀悴外表。
value.en: Your Majesty in the honor of ten thousand chariots treads the rites of a commoner—coarse mat and straw padding, drinking water and eating coarse food, sorrow swelling within, emaciation showing without.
value.literal: Your Majesty in the honor of ten thousand chariots treads the rites of a commoner—coarse mat and straw padding, drinking water and eating coarse food, sorrow swelling within, emaciation showing without.

value.en: Yet you personally toil at myriad threads of state, sit awaiting dawn, humble your heart to receive subordinates, and lean so far you have no leisure to eat—such labor of strength is extreme.
value.literal: Yet you personally toil at myriad threads of state, sit awaiting dawn, humble your heart to receive subordinates, and lean so far you have no leisure to eat—such labor of strength is extreme.

value.zh: 是以臣等悚息不寧，誠懼神氣用損，以疚大事。
value.en: Therefore we your servants tremble and breathe uneasily, truly fearing that spirit will be depleted and the great affair harmed.
value.literal: Therefore we your servants tremble and breathe uneasily, truly fearing that spirit will be depleted and the great affair harmed.

value.zh: 輒敕有司，改坐復常，率由舊典。
value.en: We dare order the relevant offices to restore your seat and routine, following the old canons.

value.zh: 惟陛下察納愚款，以慰皇太后之心。」

value.zh: 三年之喪，自古達禮，誠聖人稱情立衷，明恕而行也。
value.en: Three years' mourning has from antiquity been the penetrating rite of the realm; truly the sages weighed human feeling, set the inner mean, and acted with enlightened forbearance.
value.literal: Three years' mourning has from antiquity been the penetrating rite of the realm; truly the sages weighed human feeling, set the inner mean, and acted with enlightened forbearance.

value.zh: 神靈日遠，無所訴告，雖薄於情，食旨服美，所不堪也。
value.en: The spirits grow daily more distant; there is nowhere to cry complaint—though the outward show be slight, to taste rich food and wear fine cloth is unbearable.
value.literal: The spirits grow daily more distant; there is nowhere to cry complaint—though the outward show be slight, to taste rich food and wear fine cloth is unbearable.

value.zh: 不宜反覆，重傷其心，言用斷絕，柰何！
value.en: You ought not go back and forth and doubly wound this heart; I break off words—what can be done!

value.en: With that he carried the full three-year vigil despite every plea.

value.en: Eastern Jin nobles only began tomb pilgrimages after Sima Rui's death.
value.literal: After the move south of the Yangzi, not until Emperor Yuan died did high nobles begin visiting mausoleums to announce their leave-takings.

value.zh: 蓋由眷同友執，率情而舉，非洛京之舊也。
value.en: The practice sprang from camaraderie's impulse, not old capital law.
value.literal: They acted from private friendship among peers, not from Luoyang precedent.

value.zh: 成帝時，中宮亦年年拜陵，議者以為非禮，於是遂止，以為永制。
value.en: Cheng's harem stopped annual tomb trips once ritualists objected.
value.literal: Under Emperor Cheng the inner palace yearly visited tombs until critics called it uncanonical; the court then banned it permanently.

value.zh: 至穆帝時，褚太后臨朝，又拜陵，帝幼故也。
value.en: Mu's regent mother revived the visits while the sovereign was a child.
value.literal: Under Emperor Mu, Empress Dowager Chu regent, tombs were visited again because the boy emperor was young.

value.zh: 至孝武崩，驃騎將軍司馬道子曰：「今雖權制釋服，至於朔望諸節，自應展情陵所，以一周為斷。」
value.en: After Xiaowu died, Sima Daozi said: "Though we have shortened mourning by expedient rule, on new and full moons and festivals we should still show feeling at the tomb—take one round as the limit."
value.literal: After Xiaowu died, Sima Daozi said: "Though we have shortened mourning by expedient rule, on new and full moons and festivals we should still show feeling at the tomb—take one round as the limit."

value.zh: 於是至陵，變服單衣，煩黷無準，非禮意也。
value.en: The result was slovenly dress and chaotic etiquette at every visit.
value.literal: Thereupon courtiers went to the tombs in thin single garments—endless fuss with no standard, contrary to ritual intent.

value.zh: 及安帝元興元年，尚書左僕射桓謙奏：「百僚拜陵，起于中興，非晉舊典，積習生常，遂為近法。
value.en: In the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An, Huan Qian, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, memorialized, "The hundred officials paying respects at the mausoleum began with the Restoration and was not an old Jin statute. Accumulated practice produced a norm, and it consequently became a recent rule.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An, Huan Qian, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, memorialized, "The hundred officials paying respects at the mausoleum began with the Restoration and was not an old Jin statute. Accumulated practice produced a norm, and it consequently became a recent rule.

value.zh: 尋武皇帝詔，乃不使人主諸王拜陵，豈唯百僚！
value.en: Review Emperor Wu's edict: he forbade even the sovereign and princes from tomb visits—let alone mere officials!
value.literal: Review Emperor Wu's edict: he forbade even the sovereign and princes from tomb visits—let alone mere officials!

value.zh: 謂宜遵奉。」
value.en: We ought to obey that precedent."
value.literal: We ought to obey that precedent."

value.zh: 於是施行。
value.en: The ban took effect.
value.literal: The measure was implemented.

value.zh: 及義熙初，又復江左之舊，
value.en: Yixi reopened tomb pilgrimages for a time.
value.literal: Early in the Yixi era the southern custom briefly returned.

value.zh: 《五經通義》以為有德則諡善，無德則諡惡，故雖君臣可同。
value.en: "Tongyi of the Five Classics" holds that if one is virtuous, the posthumous title will be good, and if there is no virtue, the posthumous title will be evil, so although the emperor and his ministers can be the same.
value.literal: "Tongyi of the Five Classics" holds that if one is virtuous, the posthumous title will be good, and if there is no virtue, the posthumous title will be evil, so although the emperor and his ministers can be the same.

value.zh: 魏朝初諡''『宣帝為文侯，景王為武侯』''，文王表不宜與二祖同，於是改諡宣文、忠武。
value.en: At the beginning of the Wei Dynasty, the posthumous titles were ""Emperor Xuan was Marquis Wen, and King Jing was Marquis Wu". It was inappropriate for King Wen to have the same title as his second ancestor, so the posthumous titles were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Wei Dynasty, the posthumous titles were ""Emperor Xuan was Marquis Wen, and King Jing was Marquis Wu". It was inappropriate for King Wen to have the same title as his second ancestor, so the posthumous titles were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.

value.zh: 至文王受晉王之號，魏帝又追命宣文為宣王，忠武為景王。
value.en: When King Wen received the title of King of Jin, Emperor Wei also appointed Xuanwen as King Xuan and Zhongwu as King Jing.
value.literal: When King Wen received the title of King of Jin, Emperor Wei also appointed Xuanwen as King Xuan and Zhongwu as King Jing.

value.zh: 太康八年十月，太常上諡故太常平陵男郭奕為景侯。
value.en: In the eighth year of Taikang, in October, Taichang was given the posthumous title, so Guo Yi, the man from Pingling, Taichang, was given the title of Marquis of Jing.
value.literal: In the eighth year of Taikang, in October, Taichang was given the posthumous title, so Guo Yi, the man from Pingling, Taichang, was given the title of Marquis of Jing.

value.zh: 有司奏云：「晉受命以來，祖宗號諡群下未有同者，故郭奕為景，與景皇同，不可聽，宜諡曰穆。」
value.en: An official report said: "Since the Jin Dynasty, there has been no one with the same posthumous title for his ancestors. Therefore, Guo Yi is the king of Jing, and he is the same as Emperor Jing. It is not acceptable to listen to him, so it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title Mu."
value.literal: An official report said: "Since the Jin Dynasty, there has been no one with the same posthumous title for his ancestors. Therefore, Guo Yi is the king of Jing, and he is the same as Emperor Jing. It is not acceptable to listen to him, so it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title Mu."

value.zh: 王濟、羊璞等並云：「夫無窮之祚，名諡不一，若皆相避，于制難全。
value.en: Wang Ji, Yang Pu, and the others all said: “In an endless imperial blessing, personal names and posthumous titles are not all the same; if all are mutually avoided, the system is hard to complete.
value.literal: Wang Ji, Yang Pu, and the others all said: “In an endless imperial blessing, personal names and posthumous titles are not all the same; if all are mutually avoided, the system is hard to complete.

value.zh: 如悉不避，復非推崇事尊之禮。
value.en: If none are avoided, that again is not the rite of exalting and serving the honored.
value.literal: If none are avoided, that again is not the rite of exalting and serving the honored.

value.zh: 宜依諱名之義，但及七廟祖宗而已，不及遷毀之廟。」
value.en: It is fitting to follow the meaning of name taboo only as far as the ancestors in the seven temples, and not extend it to temples whose tablets have been moved out or destroyed.”
value.literal: It is fitting to follow the meaning of name taboo only as far as the ancestors in the seven temples, and not extend it to temples whose tablets have been moved out or destroyed.”

value.zh: 成粲、武茂、劉訥並云：「同諡非嫌。
value.en: Cheng Can, Wu Mao and Liu Na all said, "It is not inappropriate to have the same posthumous title.
value.literal: Cheng Can, Wu Mao and Liu Na all said, "It is not inappropriate to have the same posthumous title.

value.zh: 號諡者，國之大典，所以厲時作教，經天人之遠旨也。
value.en: The person with the posthumous title is the grand ceremony of the country, so he teaches in a timely manner and obeys the distant decrees of heaven and man.
value.literal: The person with the posthumous title is the grand ceremony of the country, so he teaches in a timely manner and obeys the distant decrees of heaven and man.

value.zh: 固雖君父，義有所不隆，及在臣子，或以行顯。
value.en: Even though you are a king and father, your righteousness is not upheld, and it may be shown by your actions to your ministers.
value.literal: Even though you are a king and father, your righteousness is not upheld, and it may be shown by your actions to your ministers.

value.zh: 故能使上下邁德，罔有怠荒。
value.en: Therefore, it can bring great virtue to both the superiors and subordinates, without any laziness or neglect.
value.literal: Therefore, it can bring great virtue to both the superiors and subordinates, without any laziness or neglect.

value.zh: 臣願聖世同符堯舜，行周同諡之禮，舍漢魏近制相避之議。」
value.en: I hope that the Holy World will be the same as Yao and Shun, and that the posthumous rites of Zhou Dynasty will be the same, and that the modern system of Han and Wei will be avoided.”
value.literal: I hope that the Holy World will be the same as Yao and Shun, and that the posthumous rites of Zhou Dynasty will be the same, and that the modern system of Han and Wei will be avoided.”

value.zh: 又引周公父子同諡曰文。
value.en: He also cited Zhou Gong and his son as having the same posthumous title.
value.literal: He also cited Zhou Gong and his son as having the same posthumous title.

value.zh: 武帝詔曰：「非言君臣不可同，正以奕諡景不相當耳，宜諡曰簡。」
value.en: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "It is not necessary to say that the emperor and his ministers cannot be the same. Since the posthumous title of Yi is not commensurate with the scenery, it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title of Jian."
value.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "It is not necessary to say that the emperor and his ministers cannot be the same. Since the posthumous title of Yi is not commensurate with the scenery, it is appropriate to give him the posthumous title of Jian."

value.zh: 及太元四年，侍中王欣之表君臣之嫌同諡，尚書奏以欣之言為然。
value.en: In Taiyuan 4, Palace Attendant Wang Xinzhi objected that ruler and minister should not share a posthumous title, and the Masters of Writing endorsed his view.
value.literal: When it came to Taiyuan 4, Palace Attendant Wang Xinzhi memorialized that ruler and minister should avoid sharing the same posthumous title, and the Masters of Writing reported that Xinzhi's statement was correct.

value.zh: 詔可。
value.en: The edict can be issued.
value.literal: The edict can be issued.

value.zh: 《書》曰：「唐虞稽古，建官惟百。」
value.en: The Book of Documents says: "When Tang and Yu looked back to antiquity, they created no more than a hundred offices."
value.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Tang and Yu examined antiquity; they established offices numbering only one hundred."

value.zh: 所以獎導民萌，裁成庶政。
value.en: That was how they encouraged the people and gave shape to the affairs of state.
value.literal: By this means they encouraged and guided the common people, and brought order to every branch of government.

value.zh: 《易》曰：「天垂象，聖人則之。」
value.en: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven displays signs; the sage patterns himself on them."
value.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven hangs forth images; the sage takes them as his model."

value.zh: 執法在南宮之右，上相處端門之外，而鳥龍居位，雲火垂名，前史詳之，其以尚矣。
value.en: Justice lay to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister waited beyond the Duan Gate; bird and dragon offices held rank with cloud and fire as their emblems—prior histories lay it out clearly, and the grandeur speaks for itself.
value.literal: Law sat to the right of the Southern Palace; the chief minister took station beyond the Duan Gate; the Bird and Dragon offices held their posts, cloud and fire lending their names—earlier histories spell this out in detail, and the dignity of it is plain.

value.zh: 黃帝置三公之秩，以親黎元，少昊配九扈之名，以為農正，命重黎於天地，詔融冥於水火，則可得而言焉。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor created the Three Dukes to draw near to the people; Shaohao aligned the Nine Hu titles with agricultural oversight; Chong and Li received Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming received fire and water—and such patterns can be put into words.
value.literal: The Yellow Emperor instituted the ranks of the Three Dukes to stay close to the black-haired masses; Shaohao paired the Nine Hu bird-names with the office of director of agriculture; Chong and Li were charged with Heaven and Earth; Zhu Rong and Ming were charged with fire and water—these arrangements can indeed be described.

value.zh: 伊尹曰：「三公調陰陽，九卿通寒暑，大夫知人事，列士去其私。」
value.en: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers track the seasons; grand officers attend to human affairs; ranked officers put private interest aside."
value.literal: Yi Yin said: "The Three Dukes harmonize yin and yang; the Nine Ministers watch cold and heat; grand officers understand human affairs; ranked officers rid themselves of selfishness."

value.zh: 而成湯居亳，初置二相，以伊尹、仲虺為之，凡厥樞會，仰承君命。
value.en: When Tang of Shang made Bo his seat, he first set up two chancellors—Yi Yin and Zhong Hui—and on every pivot they carried out the sovereign's will.
value.literal: When Cheng Tang ruled from Bo, he first created two chancellors and appointed Yi Yin and Zhong Hui to them; on every critical matter they looked upward to receive the ruler's commands.

value.zh: 總及周武下車，成康垂則，六卿分職，二公弘化，咸樹司存，各題標準，苟非其道，人弗虛榮。
value.en: Under King Wu and the models left by Cheng and Kang, the Six Ministers split the labor, the Two Dukes carried royal influence abroad, every bureau had its charter, and no one claimed idle honors without the right conduct.
value.literal: Altogether, when King Wu of Zhou stepped down from his chariot to rule, Cheng and Kang handed down norms; the Six Ministers divided duties; the Two Dukes spread transformation; each office kept its place and measure; if it were not the proper Way, people did not vainly seek glory.

value.zh: 貽厥孫謀，其固本也如此。
value.en: They anchored the dynasty by planning for generations yet unborn.
value.literal: They left plans for their descendants; thus they secured the foundation.

value.zh: 及秦變周官，漢遵嬴舊，或隨時適用，或因務遷革，霸王之典，義在於斯，既獲厥安，所謂得其時制者也。
value.en: Qin refashioned Zhou's bureaucracy; Han largely kept Qin's frame while tweaking it for the moment—the logic of strong rule was there—and stability meant institutions matched their age.
value.literal: When Qin altered the Zhou offices and Han followed the Ying-clan precedent, sometimes adapting to the times, sometimes shifting with practical needs—the norms of hegemons and kings lay herein; once stability was gained, this is what is called obtaining timely institutions.

value.zh: 四征興於漢代，四安起于魏初，四鎮通於柔遠，四平止於喪亂，其渡遼、淩江，輕車、強弩，式揚遐外，用表攻伐，興而復毀，厥號彌繁。
value.en: Han invented the Four Expeditions; Wei at its outset the Four Pacifications; Four Garrisons stretched toward distant peoples; Four Peace posts vanished when chaos returned. Epithets like Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow brandished force beyond the borders for campaigns—created, scrapped, then multiplied until the catalogue grew tangled.
value.literal: The Four Expeditions arose in Han; the Four Pacifications began at the start of Wei; the Four Garrisons reached outward to soothe the distant; the Four Peace offices ended with turmoil and disorder; as for Crossing-the-Liao, River-Fording, light chariot, and strong crossbow—they displayed might afar and signaled campaigns—raised up and then abolished, their titles grew ever more numerous.

value.zh: 及當塗得志，克平諸夏，初有軍師祭酒，參掌戎律。
value.en: Once the Cao regime triumphed and pacified the heartland, it introduced the army adviser libationer to share oversight of military law.
value.literal: When the house at Dangtu achieved its ambition and subdued the Central Plain, there first appeared the army adviser libationer, who jointly handled military regulations.

value.zh: 建安十三年，罷漢台司，更置丞相，而以曹公居之，用兼端揆。
value.en: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an (208), the Han ministerial posts were abolished, the chancellorship was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.
value.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, the Han terrace ministers were abolished; the chancellor was reinstated, and Lord Cao held it, thereby combining the highest civil authority.

value.zh: 孫吳、劉蜀，多依漢制，雖復臨時命氏，而無忝舊章。
value.en: Wu and Shu largely kept Han models; occasional improvised titles notwithstanding, they stayed within the classical mold.
value.literal: Eastern Wu and Liu Bei's Shu largely followed Han institutions; though they sometimes improvised titles on the spot, they did not shame the old statutes.

value.zh: 世祖武皇帝即位之初，以安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅，王祥為太保，司馬望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，世所謂八公同辰，攀雲附翼者也。
value.en: At his accession, Emperor Wu named Sima Fu Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang Grand Guardian, Sima Wang Minister of War, He Zeng Minister of Education, Xun Yi Minister of Works, Shi Bao Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian Grand General—the storied eight dukes of a single hour, men who rose by riding imperial favor.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu the Shizu first ascended the throne, he appointed Prince Fu of Anping as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang as Grand Guardian, Sima Wang as Minister of War, He Zeng as Minister of Education, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian as Grand General—what the age called the eight dukes sharing one hour, climbing clouds and attaching wings.

value.zh: 若乃成乎棟宇，非一枝之勢；
value.en: Raising the whole hall takes more than one timber;
value.literal: As for completing roof-beams and rafters—it is not the strength of a single branch;

value.zh: 處乎經綸，稱萬夫之敵。
value.en: true stewardship of the realm earns the title match for ten thousand.
value.literal: to dwell in ordering the realm is to be called a match for ten thousand men.

value.zh: 或牽羊以葉於夢，或垂釣以申其道，或空桑以獻其術，或操版以啟其心。
value.en: Some arrived through dreams of sheep and grain; some through fishing metaphors; some from humble soil with a craft to sell; some by presenting the royal tablet and winning trust.
value.literal: Some led sheep and answered a leaf in a dream; some angled with a hook to proclaim their Way; some offered their arts from an empty mulberry; some grasped the tablet to open the ruler's mind.

value.zh: 臥龍飛鴻，方金擬璧，秦奚、鄭產，楚材晉用，斯亦曩時之良具，其又昭彰者焉。
value.en: Hidden dragons and soaring swans, talents weighed like gold against jade—Qin Xi, Zheng Chan, and Chu talent employed by Jin: these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.
value.literal: The sleeping dragon, the soaring wild goose—square metal compared to round jade; the shepherd of Qin, the prodigy of Zheng; Chu talent employed by Jin—these too were fine instruments of former times, and no less manifest.

value.zh: 宣王既誅曹爽，政由己出，網羅英俊，以備天官。
value.en: After Sima Yi eliminated Cao Shuang, he ruled in his own name and stocked every court post with talent.
value.literal: Once Prince Xuan had executed Cao Shuang, government proceeded from himself alone; he gathered capable men to fill the celestial offices.

value.zh: 及蘭卿受羈，貴公顯戮，雖復策名魏氏，而乃心皇晉。
value.en: When fine officers were seized and great nobles died in public execution, names might still stand with Wei but hearts had already turned to Jin.
value.literal: When worthy ministers were placed under restraint and eminent dukes suffered public execution—though they still bore registration under the Wei, their hearts were with the august Jin.

value.zh: 及文王纂業，初啟晉台，始置二衛，有前驅養由之弩；
value.en: When Sima Zhao extended the family work and founded the Jin apparatus, he created the Two Guards with vanguard crossbows worthy of Yang Youji.
value.literal: When King Wen continued the enterprise and first opened the Jin terrace, he began setting up the Two Guards, including front-vanguard crossbows like Yang Youji's.

value.zh: 及設三部，有熊渠佽飛之眾。
value.en: When the Three Corps were established, there were masses like those of Xiong Qu and Ci Fei.
value.literal: When the Three Departments were established, there were masses like the royal swimmers of Xiong Qu.

value.zh: 是以武帝龍飛，乘茲奮翼，猶武王以周之十亂而理殷民者也。
value.en: Thus Emperor Wu's rise—vaulting on these preparations—matched King Wu deploying his ten able assistants to rule the former Shang subjects.
value.literal: Therefore when Emperor Wu ascended like a dragon, riding this to beat his wings, it was like King Wu of Zhou using the Zhou's ten ministers to govern the Yin people.

value.zh: 是以泰始盡于太康，喬柯茂葉，來居斯位；
value.en: From the Taishi era through Taikang, imposing figures filled those ranks;
value.literal: Thus from Taishi through Taikang, tall trees with lush foliage came to occupy these posts;

value.zh: 自太興訖於建元，南金北銑，用處茲秩。
value.en: from Daxing to Jianyuan, the finest metal south and north filled those offices.
value.literal: from Daxing down to Jianyuan, southern gold and northern ore were employed in these ranks.

value.zh: 雖未擬乎夔拊龍言，天工人代，亦庶幾乎任官惟賢，蒞事惟能者也。
value.en: They fell short of the sage-kings' marriage of Heaven's work to human agency, yet they neared the ideal: office by virtue, tasks by competence.
value.literal: Though they did not equal Kui's drumming and Long's pronouncements—Heaven's work and man's substitute—they approximated appoint officials only for worth, approach affairs only by ability.

value.zh: 光祿大夫假銀章青綬者，品秩第三，位在金紫將軍下，諸卿上。
value.en: Silver-blue Splendid Luminaries ranked third—below gold-purple generals but above ordinary ministers.
value.literal: Splendid luminaries grandees with silver seal and blue ribbon were grade three, below gold-purple generals and above the various ministers.

value.zh: 漢時所置無定員，多以為拜假賵贈之使，及監護喪事。
value.en: Han used them flexibly—often as ceremonial envoys or funeral supervisors.
value.literal: In Han there was no fixed quota; they were often used as envoys for investitures, gifts, and funeral oversight.

value.zh: 魏氏已來，轉復優重，不復以為使命之官。
value.en: After Wei they became honorific rather than errand posts.
value.literal: Since Wei they grew steadily weightier and ceased to be mere mission offices.

value.zh: 其諸公告老者，皆家拜此位；
value.en: Retiring dukes typically received this title by domestic edict;
value.literal: When various dukes retired, they were all appointed to this rank at home;

value.zh: 及在朝顯職，復用加之，及晉受命，仍舊不改，復以為優崇之制。
value.en: Active ministers might earn it too; Jin kept the practice as a mark of esteem.
value.literal: and for prominent posts at court it was again conferred; when Jin received the mandate it continued unchanged, again treating it as a system of honor.

value.zh: 而諸公遜位，不復加之，或更拜上公，或以本封食公祿。
value.en: Stepping-down dukes did not receive it again—some became upper dukes, others lived on fief income.
value.literal: But when dukes yielded office they were not given it again; some were promoted to upper duke, some drew duke stipends from their original fiefs.

value.zh: 其諸卿尹中朝大官年老致仕者，及內外之職加此者，前後甚眾。
value.en: Many retired ministers and officials inside and outside received it.
value.literal: Among ministers and capital officials who retired for age, and inner and outer posts given this rank, there were very many over time.

value.zh: 由是或因得開府，或進加金章紫綬，又復以為禮贈之位。
value.en: Some parlayed it into a headquarters appointment or gold-purple rank; it doubled as a ceremonial posthumous grade.
value.literal: Hence some thereby gained headquarters, some advanced to gold seal and purple ribbon; it also served as a courtesy gift rank.

value.zh: 泰始中，唯太子詹事楊珧加給事中光祿大夫。
value.en: During Taishi only Yang Yao combined household supervisor with attendant-within and Splendid Luminaries.
value.literal: In Taishi only Yang Yao, supervisor of the heir apparent's household, was additionally appointed attendant-within and splendid luminaries grandee.

value.zh: 加兵之制，諸所供給依三品將軍。
value.en: Military add-ons followed third-rank general perquisites.
value.literal: For systems with added military authority, all provisions followed third-grade generals.

value.zh: 其餘自如舊制，終武、惠、孝懷三世。
value.en: The rest followed the old regulations through the three reigns of Wu, Hui, and Xiaohuai.
value.literal: The rest followed old regulations through the reigns of Wu, Hui, and Xiaohuai.

value.zh: 秘書監，案漢桓帝延熹二年置秘書監，後省。
value.en: Han Huan created a library director in 159 CE; the seat later vanished.
value.literal: Director of the Palace Library—in tradition Emperor Huan of Han in the second year of Yanxi established a Palace Library director; later it was cut.

value.zh: 魏武為魏王，置秘書令、丞。
value.en: Cao Cao as Wei prince named a secretary director and deputy for archives.
value.literal: Wei Emperor Wu as Prince of Wei established Palace Secretary director and assistant.

value.zh: 及文帝黃初初，置中書令，典尚書奏事，而秘書改令為監。
value.en: Huangchu split drafting from archives: Zhongshu handled memorials while the old secretary director became library supervisor.
value.literal: When Wendi at the start of Huangchu established Palace Secretariat director to manage Secretariat memorial business, the Palace Secretary director title was changed to supervisor.

value.zh: 後以何禎為秘書丞，而秘書先自有丞，乃以禎為秘書右丞。
value.en: He Zhen became library deputy while a deputy already existed—so he took the new right-deputy slot.
value.literal: Later He Zhen was appointed Palace Library assistant, but the library already had an assistant; therefore Zhen was made Right Assistant of the Palace Library.

value.zh: 及晉受命，武帝以秘書並中書省，其秘書著作之局不廢。
value.en: Wudi folded library staff into the Zhongshu apparatus but kept the historiography office alive.
value.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu merged the Palace Library with the Palace Secretariat bureau, yet the library composition bureau was not abolished.

value.zh: 惠帝永平中，復置秘書監，其屬官有丞，有郎，並統著作省。
value.en: Huidi revived the library supervisor with deputies and gentlemen running the composition wing.
value.literal: Under Emperor Hui in the Yongping era the Palace Library supervisor was restored; subordinate offices included assistants and gentlemen, jointly overseeing the Composition Bureau.

value.zh: 著作郎，周左史之任也。
value.en: The compiler post echoed Zhou's left historian.
value.literal: Composition gentleman—it was the duty of Zhou's left historian.

value.zh: 漢東京圖籍在東觀，故使名儒著作東觀，有其名，尚未有官。
value.en: In Eastern Han, maps and registers were kept in the Eastern Observatory, so famed scholars wrote there; the title existed in name, but not yet as an office.
value.literal: In Eastern Han, maps and registers were kept in the Eastern Observatory, so famed scholars were made to compose works in the Eastern Observatory; the name existed, but there was not yet an official post.

value.zh: 魏明帝太和中，詔置著作郎，於此始有其官，隸中書省。
value.en: Wei Mingdi minted the composition gentleman title under Zhongshu.
value.literal: Wei Mingdi in the Taihe era issued an edict establishing composition gentlemen—here it first became an office, subordinate to the Palace Secretariat.

value.zh: 及晉受命，武帝以繆徵為中書著作郎。
value.en: Wudi named Miao Zheng as Zhongshu compiler.
value.literal: When Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu appointed Miao Zheng as Palace Secretariat composition gentleman.

value.zh: 元康二年，詔曰：「著作舊屬中書，而秘書既典文籍，今改中書著作為秘書著作。」
value.en: In the second year of Yuankang an edict said: "Composition formerly belonged to the Palace Secretariat; since the Palace Library already manages documents, now change Palace Secretariat composition to Palace Library composition."
value.literal: In the second year of Yuankang an edict said: "Composition formerly belonged to the Palace Secretariat; since the Palace Library already manages documents, now change Palace Secretariat composition to Palace Library composition."

value.zh: 於是改隸秘書省。
value.en: Compilers henceforth answered to the library bureau.
value.literal: Thus they were reassigned to the Palace Library bureau.

value.zh: 後別自置省而猶隸秘書。
value.en: They eventually spun up a dedicated bureau still under library oversight.
value.literal: Later they separately established a bureau yet still reported to the Palace Library.

value.zh: 著作郎一人，謂之大著作郎，專掌史任，又置佐著作郎八人。
value.en: One chief compiler ran history with eight assistants.
value.literal: One composition gentleman was called senior composition gentleman, solely handling historical duty; eight assistant composition gentlemen were also appointed.

value.zh: 著作郎始到職，必撰名臣傳一人。
value.en: New compilers opened their tenure by drafting a notable minister biography.
value.literal: When composition gentlemen first took office they had to compose one biography of a celebrated minister.

value.zh: 晉初承魏制，置博士十九人。
value.en: Early Jin kept nineteen classical chairs from Wei.
value.literal: Early Jin inherited Wei regulations and established nineteen erudites.

value.zh: 及咸甯四年，武帝初立國子學，定置國子祭酒、博士各一人，助教十五人，以教生徒。
value.en: 278 CE launched the academy with one libationer, one professor, and fifteen assistants teaching disciples.
value.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning Emperor Wu first founded the Imperial Academy, fixing one libationer and one erudite each, fifteen teaching assistants, to instruct students.

value.zh: 博士皆取履行清淳，通明典義者，若散騎常侍、中書侍郎、太子中庶子以上，乃得召試。
value.en: Candidates needed pristine résumés and canonical mastery; only senior attendants and above sat the exam.
value.literal: Erudites were all drawn from men of pure conduct who mastered canonical meaning; only those ranked elite cavalry standing attendant, Palace Secretariat deputy, heir-apparent household attendant or higher could be summoned to examination.

value.zh: 及江左初，減為九人。
value.en: South of the river the corps shrank to nine chairs.
value.literal: Early east of the Yangzi it was reduced to nine.

value.zh: 元帝末，增《儀禮》、《春秋公羊》博士各一人，合為十一人。
value.en: Late Yuandi added Etiquette and Gongyang chairs—eleven professors.
value.literal: At the end of Emperor Yuan's reign one Ceremonies erudite each was added for Etiquette and Gongyang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, totaling eleven.

value.zh: 後又增為十六人，不復分掌《五經》，而謂之太學博士也。
value.en: The roster grew to sixteen unified professors rather than one canon each.
value.literal: Later it was increased to sixteen; they no longer split custody of the Five Classics but were called Imperial Academy erudites.

value.zh: 孝武太元十年，損國子助教員為十人。
value.en: 385 CE trimmed academy assistants to ten.
value.literal: Emperor Xiaowu in the tenth year of Taiyuan cut Imperial Academy assistant posts to ten.

value.zh: 言之不從，是謂不乂
value.en: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.
value.literal: When commands find no compliance, the canon calls it a failure of proper order.

value.zh: 魏時起安世殿，武帝后居之。
value.en: Wei builders raised Anshi Hall, later occupied by Sima Yan's empress.
value.literal: In Wei they built Anshi Hall; later the empress of Emperor Wu resided there.

value.zh: 安世，武帝字也。
value.en: The hall bore Sima Yan's childhood name, Anshi.
value.literal: Anshi was Emperor Wu's courtesy name.

value.zh: 武帝每延群臣，多說平生常事，未嘗及經國遠圖。
value.en: At court he dwelt on small talk, never on how to steer the empire.
value.literal: Whenever Emperor Wu extended audiences to ministers he spoke mostly of trivial personal matters and never touched long-term state plans.

value.zh: 此言之不從也。
value.en: It marked another omen of rulers who would not voice the nation's business.
value.literal: This was a case of words not following what duty required.

value.zh: 何曾謂子遵曰：「國家無貽厥之謀，及身而已，後嗣其殆乎！
value.en: He Ceng said to his son Zun: "The state has no plan to hand down its legacy; it will exhaust itself in this generation — will not posterity be endangered?
value.literal: He Ceng said to his son Zun: "The state has no plan to hand down its legacy; it will exhaust itself in this generation — will not posterity be endangered?

value.zh: 此子孫之憂也。」
value.en: That is posterity's worry."
value.literal: That is posterity's worry."

value.zh: 自永熙後王室漸亂，永嘉中天下大壞，及何綏以非辜被殺，皆如曾言。
value.en: From Yongxi onward the clan unraveled; Yongjia's catastrophe and He Sui's unjust death fulfilled his prophecy.
value.literal: After Yongxi the royal house slid into disorder; in Yongjia the realm shattered; when He Sui was killed without guilt — all happened as Ceng had said.

value.zh: 武帝初，何曾薄太官御膳，自取私食，子劭又過之，而王愷又過劭。
value.en: He Zeng snubbed the palace chefs for home cooking; He Shao and Wang Kai escalated the indulgence.
value.literal: Early in Emperor Wu's reign He Zeng scorned the imperial kitchen and took private food; his son Shao exceeded him, and Wang Kai exceeded Shao.

value.zh: 王愷、羊琇之儔，盛致聲色，窮珍極麗。
value.en: Wang Kai and Yang Xiu bankrolled musicians, concubines, and luxuries without limit.
value.literal: Wang Kai, Yang Xiu, and their ilk lavished music and women, exhausting treasures and utmost beauty.

value.zh: 至元康中，誇恣成俗，轉相高尚，石崇之侈，遂兼王、何，而儷人主矣。
value.en: Under Yuankang, ostentation turned into fashion until Shi Chong outspent even Wang Kai and He Zeng, shadowing the throne itself.
value.literal: By the Yuankang years extravagance had become custom; people vied to outdo one another; Shi Chong's luxury surpassed Wang and He combined and rivaled the sovereign.

value.zh: 崇既誅死，天下尋亦淪喪。
value.en: Shi Chong's death presaged the empire's swift collapse.
value.literal: After Chong was executed and killed, the realm soon also fell into ruin.

value.zh: 僭逾之咎也。
value.en: The historians chalked it up to rank-breaking excess.
value.literal: This was the fault of presumption and overstepping.

value.zh: 武帝泰始七年五月閏月旱，大雩。
value.en: Sima Yan's Taihe 7 intercalary fifth month brought another da yu season.
value.literal: Emperor Wu — intercalary fifth month drought; great yu.

value.zh: 泰始八年五月，旱。
value.en: the eighth year of Taishi's fifth month stayed rainless.
value.literal: Fifth month of the eighth year — drought.

value.zh: 是時帝納荀勖邪說，留賈充不復西鎮，而任愷漸疏，上下皆蔽之應也。
value.en: Bad faith at court — Xun Xu's whispering, Jia Chong's stalled western posting, Ren Kai sidelined — mirrored blocked communication.
value.literal: At that time the emperor accepted Xun Xu's vicious counsel, kept Jia Chong at court instead of sending him west again, and Ren Kai grew estranged — an omen of high and low both blocked.

value.zh: 及李憙、魯芝、李胤等並在散職，近厥德不用之謂也。
value.en: Worthy men languished in sinecures while mediocrities ran policy.
value.literal: Moreover Li Xi, Lu Zhi, Li Yin and others all held idle posts — close to "desired virtue unused."

value.zh: 孫皓天紀中，童謠曰：「阿童復阿童，銜刀游渡江。
value.en: Under Sun Hao's Tianji years a rhyme said: "Atong again Atong, biting a blade he swims the river.
value.literal: Under Sun Hao's Tianji years a rhyme said: "Atong again Atong, biting a blade he swims the river.

value.zh: 不畏岸上獸，但畏水中龍。」
value.en: Fear not beasts on the bank — only fear the dragon in the water."
value.literal: Fear not beasts on the bank — only fear the dragon in the water."

value.zh: 武帝聞之，加王浚龍驤將軍。
value.en: Sima Yan ennobled Wang Jun as "dragon" general on cue.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu heard it, he promoted Wang Jun to Dragon-Loft general.

value.zh: 及征吳，江西眾軍無過者，而王浚先定秣陵。
value.en: Wang Jun's flotilla outran every rival to seize Nanjing.
value.literal: When Wu was attacked, no western army surpassed his; Wang Jun first took Moling.

value.zh: 武帝太康三年平吳後，江南童謠曰：「局縮肉，數橫目，中國當敗吳當復。」
value.en: After Emperor Wu pacified Wu in Taikang 3, a children’s rhyme south of the Yangtze said, “Shriveled flesh, several horizontal eyes; the Middle Kingdom shall be defeated, Wu shall be restored.”
value.literal: After Emperor Wu pacified Wu in Taikang 3, a children’s rhyme south of the Yangtze said, “Shriveled flesh, several horizontal eyes; the Middle Kingdom shall be defeated, Wu shall be restored.”

value.zh: 又曰：「宮門柱，且當朽，吳當復，在三十年後。」
value.en: It also said: "Palace gate pillars will rot; Wu returns in thirty years."
value.literal: It also said: "Palace gate pillars will rot; Wu returns in thirty years."

value.zh: 又曰：「雞鳴不拊翼，吳復不用力。」
value.en: It also said: "Crows crow without folding wings — Wu needs hardly lift a finger."
value.literal: It also said: "Crows crow without folding wings — Wu needs hardly lift a finger."

value.zh: 于時吳人皆謂在孫氏子孫，故竊發為亂者相繼。
value.en: Locals read the lines as Sun clan prophecy and rebelled in waves.
value.literal: Then Wu people all thought it meant Sun heirs, so secret risings followed one another.

value.zh: 案「橫目」者四字，自吳亡至元帝興幾四十年，元帝興于江東，皆如童謠之言焉。
value.en: Note: "horizontal eyes" forms the graph for "four"; from Wu's fall to Yuan-di's rise in the east was nearly forty years — all matched the rhymes.
value.literal: Note: "horizontal eyes" forms the graph for "four"; from Wu's fall to Yuan-di's rise in the east was nearly forty years — all matched the rhymes.

value.zh: 元帝懦而少斷，「局縮肉」者，有所斥也。
value.en: Yuan-di was timid and indecisive; "shriveled meat" rebukes that weakness.
value.literal: Yuan-di was timid and indecisive; "shriveled meat" rebukes that weakness.

value.zh: 惠帝永熙中，河內溫縣有人如狂，造書曰：「光光文長，大戟為牆。
value.en: Under Emperor Hui's Yongxi years, a man in Wen county, Henan, raved like a madman and wrote: "Bright bright Wen-chang — halberds for walls.
value.literal: Under Emperor Hui's Yongxi years, a man in Wen county, Henan, raved like a madman and wrote: "Bright bright Wen-chang — halberds for walls.

value.zh: 毒藥雖行，戟還自傷。」
value.en: Though poison runs its course, halberds wound themselves."
value.literal: Though poison runs its course, halberds wound themselves."

value.zh: 又曰：「兩火沒地，哀哉秋蘭。
value.en: It also said: "Two fires sink into earth — alas, autumn orchid.
value.literal: It also said: "Two fires sink into earth — alas, autumn orchid.

value.zh: 歸形街郵，終為人歎。」
value.en: Form returns to the roadside post — in the end men sigh over you."
value.literal: Form returns to the roadside post — in the end men sigh over you."

value.zh: 及楊駿居內府，以戟為衛，死時又為戟所害傷。
value.en: Yang Jun's halberd corps foretold his own skewering.
value.literal: When Yang Jun dwelt in the inner palace he used halberds for guards; at death he was again wounded by halberds.

value.zh: 楊後被廢，賈后絕其膳八日而崩，葬街郵亭北，百姓哀之也。
value.en: Consort Yang died of Jia Nanfeng's hunger strike and was dumped by the courier station.
value.literal: Empress Yang was deposed; Empress Jia starved her eight days until she died; she was buried north of Jieyou post; the people pitied her.

value.zh: 雨火，武帝諱，蘭，楊後字也。
value.en: Commentators read the paired "fire" graphs as alluding to Emperor Wu's taboo name and "orchid" as Empress Yang Zhi's style name.
value.literal: "Two fires" is Emperor Wu's taboo graph; "orchid" was Empress Yang's style name.

value.zh: 其時又有童謠曰：「二月末，三月初，荊筆楊板行詔書，宮中大馬幾作驢。」
value.en: Then another rhyme ran: "Late second month, early third — Jing brush and Yang tablet carry edicts; the palace's great horse nearly becomes a donkey."
value.literal: Then another rhyme ran: "Late second month, early third — Jing brush and Yang tablet carry edicts; the palace's great horse nearly becomes a donkey."

value.zh: 此時楊駿專權，楚王用事，故言「荊筆楊板」。
value.en: At that time Yang Jun monopolized authority and the Prince of Chu held sway — hence "Jing brush and Yang tablet."
value.literal: At that time Yang Jun monopolized authority and the Prince of Chu held sway — hence "Jing brush and Yang tablet."

value.zh: 二人不誅，則君臣禮悖，故云「幾作驢」也。
value.en: If the two were not executed, ruler-minister ritual would invert — hence "nearly a donkey."
value.literal: If the two were not executed, ruler-minister ritual would invert — hence "nearly a donkey."

value.zh: 武帝太康九年，幽州有犬，鼻行地三百餘步。
value.en: In Taikang 9 under Emperor Wu, a Youzhou dog was said to nose-walk more than three hundred paces.
value.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 9 — in Youzhou there was a dog that walked more than three hundred paces with its nose to the ground.

value.zh: 天戒若曰，是時帝不思和嶠之言，卒立惠帝，以致衰亂，是言不從之罰也。
value.en: The freak dog echoed Sima Yan's refusal to change the heir.
value.literal: Heaven's warning: then the emperor ignored He Jiao's advice, finally enthroned Emperor Hui, inviting decay — punishment for heedless words.

value.zh: 武帝太康五年五月丁巳，隕石于溫及河陽各二。
value.en: On dingsi in the fifth month of Taikang 5, two meteorites fell at Wen and two at Heyang.
value.literal: Emperor Wu, Taikang 5, fifth month, dingsi — two meteorites each fell at Wen and Heyang.

value.zh: 六年正月，隕石于溫，三。
value.en: A second fall hit Wen commandery.
value.literal: Sixth year first month — meteorites at Wen, three.

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 後為貴嬪，姿陋無寵，以才德見禮。
value.en: Raised to honorable lady despite plain looks, she won respect through wit and character.
value.literal: Later she became honorable lady—plain in looks without favor, honored for talent and virtue.

value.zh: 體羸多患，常居薄室，帝每遊華林，輒回輦過之。
value.en: Frail and sickly, she kept to spare rooms; each imperial outing to Splendid Grove detoured past her lodge.
value.literal: Her frame frail and often ill, she dwelt in modest chambers; whenever the emperor toured Splendid Grove he turned his carriage to pass her gate.

value.zh: 言及文義，辭對清華，左右侍聽，莫不稱美。
value.en: Her answers on texts sparkled; every listener praised her grace.
value.literal: When discourse touched literary meaning her replies were lucid and splendid; attendants left and right listened—none failed to praise.

value.zh: 惟泰始十年秋七月丙寅，晉元皇后楊氏崩，嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: On that summer day in 274 Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!
value.literal: On the bingyin day of autumn in the seventh month of the tenth Taishi year the Jin primal empress Lady Yang died—alas!

value.zh: 昔有莘適殷，姜姒歸周，宣德中闈，徽音永流。
value.en: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang water wed Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
value.literal: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang Si returned to Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.

value.zh: 樊衛二姬，匡齊翼楚；
value.en: Fan Ji and Wei Ji uplifted Qi and Chu;
value.literal: The two Ji ladies of Fan and Wei steadied Qi and aided Chu;

value.zh: 馬鄧兩妃，亦毗漢主。
value.en: Ma and Deng consorts beside Han sovereigns did the same.
value.literal: the two consorts Ma and Deng likewise aided Han sovereigns.

value.zh: 峨峨元后，光嬪晉宇。
value.en: Towering primal queen—you lit the Jin harem.
value.literal: Lofty primal queen—you glorified consorts of Jin.

value.zh: 伉儷聖皇，比蹤往古。
value.en: You walked beside the sage throne as queens of old.
value.literal: You matched the sage emperor—tracks aligned with ancient models.

value.zh: 遭命不永，背陽即陰。
value.en: Heaven refused long life—you crossed from light to shade.
value.literal: Heaven granted no long span—you turned from yang toward shade.

value.zh: 六宮號咷，四海慟心。
value.en: Six wings of the harem keened; all beneath Heaven tore their breasts.
value.literal: Six palaces wailed; four seas shared torn hearts.

value.zh: 嗟余鄙妾，銜恩特深。
value.en: Mean concubine though I am—your kindness pierced deepest.
value.literal: Alas, mean concubine—I bore uniquely deep grace.

value.zh: 追慕三良，甘心自沈。
value.en: I envy the three who followed Duke Mu—I would gladly sink with you.
value.literal: I chase the Three Worthies—gladly I would sink myself.

value.zh: 何用存思？
value.en: Why hoard longing?
value.literal: What use is longing?

value.zh: 不忘德音。
value.en: Keep your virtuous words alive.
value.literal: Never forget virtuous words.

value.zh: 何用紀述？
value.en: Why record deeds?
value.literal: What use is chronicling?

value.zh: 託辭翰林。
value.en: Commit them to ink and Hanlin.
value.literal: Entrust phrases to the brush grove.

value.zh: 乃作誄曰：
value.en: Thus runs her lament:
value.literal: Thus she composed the dirge, saying:

value.zh: 赫赫元后，出自有楊。
value.en: Bright primal queen—you rose from the house of Yang.
value.literal: Radiant primal queen—you sprang from Yang.

value.zh: 奕世朱輪，燿彼華陽。
value.en: Generation on generation rode vermillion wheels—Huayang blazed.
value.literal: For generations vermillion wheels gleamed—Huayang blazed.

value.zh: 惟嶽降神，顯茲禎祥。
value.en: Sacred peaks poured forth spirit—showing these blessed omens.
value.literal: The peak sent down spirits—revealing these auspicious signs.

value.zh: 篤生英媛，休有烈光。
value.en: From them sprang a heroine blazing with light.
value.literal: Earnestly was born a splendid maid—she bore radiant glory.

value.zh: 含靈握文，異于庶姜。
value.en: Spirit and letters dwelt in her—not common flesh.
value.literal: She housed spirit and grasped pattern—unlike common Jiang brides.

value.zh: 和暢春日，操厲秋霜。
value.en: Gentle as vernal sun; resolve sharp as autumn frost.
value.literal: Gentle as spring sun; carriage stern as autumn frost.

value.zh: 疾彼攸遂，敦此義方。
value.en: She spurned reckless ease and upheld righteous paths.
value.literal: She hated those who rushed heedlessly; she cherished righteous rule.

value.zh: 率由四教，匪怠匪荒。
value.en: She walked the four teachings—never idle, never wild.
value.literal: She followed the four teachings—never slack, never waste.

value.zh: 行周六親，徽音顯揚。
value.en: Among six degrees of kin her sweet fame rang.
value.literal: She moved through six kinships—fair fame rose bright.

value.zh: 顯揚伊何？
value.en: Where did her praise ring?
value.literal: Where did that fame shine?

value.zh: 京室是臧。
value.en: It rang through the royal house.
value.literal: The capital chamber held her good.

value.zh: 乃娉乃納，聿嬪聖皇。
value.en: Courtship led her to the sage sovereign’s side.
value.literal: Betrothed and welcomed—she married the sage emperor.

value.zh: 正位閨閾，惟德是將。
value.en: She ordered inner gates—virtue guided every step.
value.literal: She rectified inner thresholds—virtue led her charge.

value.zh: 鳴珮有節，發言有章。
value.en: Her pendants chimed in rhythm; every phrase wore pattern.
value.literal: Jade pendants sounded with measure; speech carried patterned grace.

value.zh: 仰觀列圖，俯覽篇籍。
value.en: She studied charts above and rolled texts below.
value.literal: She looked up to illustrated charts; bent to scan texts.

value.zh: 顧問女史，咨詢竹帛。
value.en: She queried palace scholars and silk-bound histories.
value.literal: She consulted female scribes; asked counsel of bamboo and silk.

value.zh: 思媚皇姑，虔恭朝夕。
value.en: She charmed her royal mother-in-law with dawn-and-dusk reverence.
value.literal: She sought to charm royal mother-in-law—dawn and dusk reverent.

value.zh: 允釐中饋，執事有恪。
value.en: She governed inner kitchens—every duty performed with awe.
value.literal: She truly ordered inner kitchens—each task performed with awe.

value.zh: 于禮斯勞，于敬斯勤。
value.en: Ritual bent her back; reverence drove her nights.
value.literal: In ritual she toiled; in reverence she strove.

value.zh: 雖曰齊聖，邁德日新。
value.en: Though hailed unequaled, her virtue renewed each dawn.
value.literal: Although called peerlessly holy, her virtue renewed daily.

value.zh: 日新伊何，克廣弘仁。
value.en: What did renewal bring?
value.literal: What meant daily renewal?

value.zh: 終溫且惠，帝妹是親。
value.en: Ever-kind, ever-gentle—she cherished the emperor’s own sisters.
value.literal: She widened lavish kindness—she cherished the emperor’s sisters.

value.zh: 經緯六宮，罔不彌綸。
value.en: She threaded six wings of the harem—nothing slipped her weave.
value.literal: She wove order through six palaces—nothing escaped her net.

value.zh: 群妾惟仰，譬彼北辰。
value.en: Lesser ladies looked up as to the North Star.
value.literal: Concubines looked up as to the pole star.

value.zh: 亦既青陽，鳴鳩告時。
value.en: Spring greens when turtle-doves call the hour.
value.literal: Already green spring—the turtle dove announces season.

value.zh: 躬執桑曲，率導媵姬。
value.en: She led brides with mulberry hook in hand.
value.literal: She grasped mulberry hooks herself—leading attendant brides.

value.zh: 修成蠶蔟，分繭理絲。
value.en: She tended trays, split cocoons, sorted filament.
value.literal: She finished silkworm trays—partitioned cocoons, sorted silk.

value.zh: 女工是察，祭服是治。
value.en: She inspected needlework and fashioned sacral gowns.
value.literal: She inspected women’s work—she directed ritual robes.

value.zh: 祗奉宗廟，永言孝思。
value.en: She served the temple—always mindful of filial hearts.
value.literal: She reverently served the ancestral temple—ever speaking filial thought.

value.zh: 于彼六行，靡不蹈之。
value.en: She practiced every womanly virtue.
value.literal: Of those six conducts—she trod every one.

value.zh: 皇英佐舜，塗山翼禹。
value.en: Ehuang and Nüying aided Shun; Tushan aided Yu.
value.literal: Huang and Ying aided Shun; Tushan winged Yu.

value.zh: 惟衛惟樊，二霸是輔。
value.en: Wei Ji and Fan Ji steadied two hegemons.
value.literal: Only Wei, only Fan—two hegemons relied on them.

value.zh: 明明我后，異世同矩。
value.en: Bright our queen—another age, same measure.
value.literal: Bright bright our queen—different age, same square rule.

value.zh: 亦能有亂，謀及天府。
value.en: She too could heal unrest ; she schemed with Heaven’s storehouse.
value.literal: She too could cope with turmoil ; she planned with Heaven’s treasury.

value.zh: 內敷陰教，外毗陽化。
value.en: Within she spread yin teaching; without she aided yang rule.
value.literal: Within she spread women’s teaching; without she aided yang transformation.

value.zh: 綢繆庶正，密勿夙夜。
value.en: She knit every minister—tireless day and night.
value.literal: She bound together myriad officers—diligent night and day.

value.zh: 恩從風翔，澤隨雨播。
value.en: Her grace rode wind; her bounty fell like rain.
value.literal: Grace rode the wind; bounty fell like rain.

value.zh: 中外禔福，遐邇詠歌。
value.en: Court and countryside flourished; near and far sang hymns.
value.literal: Inner and outer gained bliss—near and far sang praise.

value.zh: 惟帝與后，契闊在昔。
value.en: Emperor and queen—pledged long ago.
value.literal: Emperor and consort—long joined in ancient pledge.

value.zh: 比翼白屋，雙飛紫閣。
value.en: They nested in humble roofs—then flew paired to purple halls.
value.literal: Wing to wing from white-thatched halls—paired flight to purple towers.

value.zh: 悼后傷后，早即窀穸。
value.en: They mourn their queen—she sank too soon to stone.
value.literal: Mourning queen, wounded queen—early she entered the vault.

value.zh: 言斯既及，涕泗隕落。
value.en: Speech stops here—tears and mucus fall.
value.literal: Words reach here—tears and mucus fall.

value.zh: 追惟我后，實聰實哲。
value.en: Remembering her—truly keen, truly wise.
value.literal: Tracing my queen—truly keen, truly wise.

value.zh: 通于性命，達于儉節。
value.en: She grasped life’s truth—she mastered austerity.
value.literal: She penetrated nature and fate—she grasped thrift’s rule.

value.zh: 送終之禮，比素上世。
value.en: Her burial honored utmost thrift—plain as oldest times.
value.literal: Funeral rites matched plain antiquity—pared like highest ages.

value.zh: 襚無珍寶，唅無明月。
value.en: Her grave clothes bore no gems; no pearl filled her mouth.
value.literal: Burial garments held no treasure; mouth jewels held no bright moon-pearl.

value.zh: 潛輝梓宮，永背昭晰。
value.en: Her gleam sinks in the catalpa bier—gone from daylight forever.
value.literal: Hidden radiance in the catalpa palace—forever turned from clear light.

value.zh: 臣妾哀號，同此斷絕。
value.en: We servants keened—we shared that rupture.
value.literal: Concubines and maids wail—together cut off.

value.zh: 庭宇遏密，幽室增陰。
value.en: Courtyards fell mute; shadow thickened every room.
value.literal: Courtyard silence grows dense—dark chambers deepen shade.

value.zh: 空設幃帳，虛置衣衾。
value.en: Silken curtains hang hollow; quilts lie unused.
value.literal: Canopies stand empty—robes and quilts vainly spread.

value.zh: 人亦有言，神道難尋。
value.en: Men say ghost roads cannot be traced.
value.literal: Men also say the spirit path cannot be traced.

value.zh: 悠悠精爽，豈浮豈沈。
value.en: Her bright soul wanders—does it rise or sink?
value.literal: Far drifts her shining soul—does it float or sink?

value.zh: 豐奠日陳，冀魂之臨。
value.en: Opulent gifts pile daily—we pray her ghost approaches.
value.literal: Rich offerings daily spread—we hope the soul draws near.

value.zh: 孰云元后，不聞其音。
value.en: Who claims our primal queen hears nothing now?
value.literal: Who says the primal queen—cannot hear her voice?

value.zh: 咸寧二年，納悼后，芬于座受詔作頌，其辭曰：
value.en: In 276 they welcomed Empress Yang Zhi; Zuo Fen took orders at banquet to hymn her:
value.literal: In second Xianning they brought in Empress Dao; Fen at seat received edict to compose praise, saying:

value.zh: 翼翼聖皇，叡喆孔純。
value.en: Solemn sage emperor—pure in deepest wit.
value.literal: Solemn sage emperor—profound wisdom utterly pure.

value.zh: 愍茲狂戾，闡惠播仁。
value.en: He pitied cruel times—spread mercy everywhere.
value.literal: He pitied cruel turmoil—spread kindness and planted mercy.

value.zh: 蠲釁滌穢，與時惟新。
value.en: He washed sin away—made all things new.
value.literal: He wiped stains and washed filth—renewed with seasons.

value.zh: 沛然洪赦，恩詔遐震。
value.en: Grand amnesty rolled—edicts shook frontiers.
value.literal: Surging great amnesty—edicts shook distant shores.

value.zh: 后之踐阼，囹圄虛陳。
value.en: When she rose—jails gaped empty.
value.literal: When she mounted throne—prisons stood empty.

value.zh: 萬國齊歡，六合同欣。
value.en: Ten thousand states danced—six directions sang.
value.literal: Ten thousand lands rejoiced—six zones shared delight.

value.zh: 坤神抃舞，天人載悅。
value.en: Earth spirit dances—Heaven and mortals thrill.
value.literal: Earth goddess claps—Heaven and man rejoice.

value.zh: 興瑞降祥，表精日月。
value.en: Good omens arrive—sun and moon blaze essence.
value.literal: Omens rise—sun and moon display essence.

value.zh: 和氣煙熅，三光朗烈。
value.en: Warm vapors coil—three lights burn bright.
value.literal: Harmony veils warm mist—three luminaries blaze clear.

value.zh: 既獲嘉時，尋播甘雪。
value.en: Blessed hour brings timely snow.
value.literal: Season blessed—they soon spread sweet snow.

value.zh: 玄雲晻藹，靈液霏霏。
value.en: Purple clouds billow—spirit dew drifts.
value.literal: Dark clouds veil thick—numinous dew drifts fine.

value.zh: 既儲既積，待陽而晞。
value.en: Moisture gathers—sun must dry it.
value.literal: Stored and piled—it waits for sun to dry.

value.zh: 曣晛沾濡，柔潤中畿。
value.en: Warm vapor drenches—capital fields soften.
value.literal: Moisture soaks—soft rains central fields.

value.zh: 長享豐年，福祿永綏。
value.en: Enjoy fat harvests—wealth and peace endure.
value.literal: Long enjoy rich years—blessing and wage forever calm.

value.zh: 及帝女萬年公主薨，帝痛悼不已，詔芬為誄，其文甚麗。
value.en: When Princess Wannian died Wu mourned without cease and bid Zuo Fen write—her elegy was splendid.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu’s daughter Princess Wannian died, the emperor grieved endlessly and ordered Fen to compose a dirge—its prose extremely beautiful.

value.zh: 帝重芬詞藻，每有方物異寶，必詔為賦頌，以是屢獲恩賜焉。
value.en: He prized her lines; each tribute beast or gem won an ode—she gathered repeated gifts.
value.literal: The emperor prized Fen’s phrasing; whenever rare treasures arrived he ordered rhapsodies and hymns—thereby she repeatedly received imperial gifts.

value.zh: 答兄思詩、書及雜賦頌數十篇，並行于世。
value.en: Her replies to Zuo Si and dozens of essays circulated widely.
value.literal: Replies to brother Si’s poems, letters, and assorted rhapsodies and hymns—several tens of pieces—all circulated in the age.

value.zh: 泰始九年，帝多簡良家子女以充內職，自擇其美者以絳紗繫臂。
value.en: In 273 he drafted palace girls from good families and marked his favorites with crimson silk arm-bands.
value.literal: In ninth Taishi year the emperor broadly drafted daughters of good houses for inner service and personally tied crimson gauze on those he deemed fairest.

value.zh: 而芳既入選，下殿號泣。
value.en: Hu Fang crossed the hall weeping once chosen.
value.literal: When Fang entered selection she descended the hall weeping and crying.

value.zh: 左右止之曰：「陛下聞聲。」
value.en: Attendants hissed, “The emperor will hear.”
value.literal: Attendants beside her stopped her: “His Majesty will hear your voice.”

value.zh: 芳曰：「死且不畏，何畏陛下！」
value.en: She shot back, “I fear death itself—why fear an emperor?”
value.literal: Fang said: “I fear not death—why fear His Majesty!”

value.zh: 帝遣洛陽令司馬肇策拜芳為貴嬪。
value.en: Emperor Wu had Luoyang prefect Sima Zhao invest her with honorable rank.
value.literal: The emperor ordered Luoyang Magistrate Sima Zhao to invest Fang as honorable lady by tally.

value.zh: 帝每有顧問，不飾言辭，率爾而答，進退方雅。
value.en: Whenever he questioned her she answered straight without flourish—yet comported herself with modest grace.
value.literal: Whenever the emperor questioned her she did not polish phrases—answered plainly yet withdrew with modest grace.

value.zh: 時帝多內寵，平吳之後復納孫皓宮人數千，自此掖庭殆將萬人。
value.en: After Wu fell he absorbed thousands of Sun Hao’s girls until the harem neared ten thousand souls.
value.literal: At that time the emperor greatly favored inner chambers; after conquering Wu he took several thousand of Sun Hao’s palace women—thereafter pepper chambers neared ten thousand.

value.zh: 而並寵者甚眾，帝莫知所適，常乘羊車，恣其所之，至便宴寢。
value.en: So many favorites he rode a goat cart wherever chance led and slept there.
value.literal: Many equally favored—emperor knew not whom to choose—often rode goat-drawn cart wherever it pleased, feasting and bedding where it stopped.

value.zh: 宮人乃取竹葉插戶，以鹽汁灑地，而引帝車。
value.en: Women sprinkled salt and hung bamboo leaves to steer his goat cart.
value.literal: Palace ladies therefore inserted bamboo leaves in doors, sprinkled salt water on ground to lure emperor’s cart.

value.zh: 然芳最蒙愛幸，殆有專房之寵焉，侍御服飾亞于皇后。
value.en: Hu Fang won nearest monopoly favor—her wardrobe rivaled the empress.
value.literal: Yet Fang received deepest favor—almost exclusive chamber privilege—attendants’ robes secondary only to empress.

value.zh: 帝嘗與之摴蒱，爭矢，遂傷上指。
value.en: Playing dice for arrows she wounded his finger.
value.literal: Emperor once played chupu with her; quarreling over arrows they wounded his finger.

value.zh: 帝怒曰：「此固將種也！」
value.en: He snapped, “That’s pure warrior blood!”
value.literal: Emperor angrily said: “This truly is general stock!”

value.zh: 芳對曰：「北伐公孫，西距諸葛，非將種而何？」
value.en: She shot back, “You marched north against Gongsun and west against Zhuge—what else is warlord stock?”
value.literal: Fang replied: “North you attacked Gongsun—west you resisted Zhuge—if not general stock, what?”

value.zh: 帝甚有慚色。
value.en: He flushed with shame.
value.literal: The emperor felt deeply ashamed.

value.zh: 芳生武安公主。
value.en: She bore Princess Wu’an.
value.literal: Fang bore Princess Wu’an.

value.zh: 諸葛夫人名婉，琅邪陽都人也。
value.en: Lady Zhuge Wan came from Yangdu in Langya.
value.literal: Lady Zhuge was named Wan, a native of Yangdu in Langya.

value.zh: 父沖，字茂長，廷尉卿。
value.en: Her father Zhuge Chong, courtesy Maochang, served as Commandant of Justice.
value.literal: Her father Chong, courtesy Maochang, was Commandant of Justice.

value.zh: 婉以泰始九年春入宮，帝臨軒，使使持節、洛陽令司馬肇拜為夫人。
value.en: In spring 273 she entered court; Emperor Wu had Sima Zhao invest her as Lady from the southern gallery.
value.literal: In spring of ninth Taishi year she entered palace; emperor faced southern porch and ordered envoy with tally Luoyang Magistrate Sima Zhao to invest her as lady.

value.zh: 安平獻王孚
value.en: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.
value.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).

value.zh: 及武帝受禪，陳留王就金墉城，孚拜辭，執王手，流涕歔欷，不能自勝。
value.en: When Sima Yan took the throne the Wei emperor withdrew to Jinyong; Fu clasped his hand in farewell and wept uncontrollably.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication, the king of Chenliu went to Jinyong Fortress; Fu took leave of him, grasped the king's hand, wept and sobbed, and could not overcome himself.

value.zh: 曰：「臣死之日，固大魏之純臣也。」
value.en: He said, 'On the day I die I shall indeed be a pure minister of Great Wei.'
value.literal: He said, 'On the day I die I shall indeed be a pure minister of Great Wei.'

value.zh: 詔曰：「太傅勳德弘茂，朕所瞻仰，以光導弘訓，鎮靜宇內，願奉以不臣之禮。
value.en: An edict said, 'The Grand Mentor's merit and virtue are vast and flourishing—what I look up to; by him brilliance guides instruction and calms the realm within the four seas—I wish to accord him rites that need not treat him as subject.
value.literal: An edict said, 'The Grand Mentor's merit and virtue are vast and flourishing—what I look up to; by him brilliance guides instruction and calms the realm within the four seas—I wish to accord him rites that need not treat him as subject.

value.zh: 其封為安平王，邑四萬戶。
value.en: Enfeoff him as prince of Anping with forty thousand households.
value.literal: Enfeoff him as prince of Anping with forty thousand households.

value.zh: 進拜太宰、持節、都督中外諸軍事。」
value.en: Advance him to Grand Preceptor, bearer of credentials, and commander-in-chief of all military affairs inside and outside."
value.literal: Advance him to Grand Preceptor, bearer of credentials, and commander-in-chief of all military affairs inside and outside."

value.zh: 有司奏，諸王未之國者，所置官屬，權未有備。
value.en: Bureaus noted princes remaining at capital lacked complete households.
